views.canonical_question: In the sequential bond construction, a complete state after n emitted bits is produced by applying stage matrices in order, starting from an explicit bond boundary vector. Assume for each stage index t and each clean input column (fresh bit input = 0, bond input a) the stage entry equals the corresponding tensor core entry K t. Prove by induction on n that the full run amplitude at bit word x and final bond label b equals the matrix-vector product of the chronological transfer contraction of the cores with the boundary, (transfer K n x) applied to the boundary, read at b. State precisely which columns of the stages are therefore irrelevant.
canonical_assumptions: the only hypothesis is clean-column equality of each stage with the corresponding tensor core; no global state action is assumed
the boundary is an explicit bond vector supplied to the run
canonical_conventions: the last emitted core multiplies on the left (same order as circuit evaluation)
transfer at length 0 is the identity matrix

canonical_rubric.criterion: Handles the base case using transfer at length 0 = identity and run at length 0 = boundary.
Expands the inductive step via the clean-column collapse of one step into a sum over the bond label a.

Applies the clean-column hypothesis and the inductive hypothesis, then recognizes the sum as coreSlice(K n)(x(last)) times the length-n transfer-applied-to-boundary, i.e. transfer K (n+1) x applied to boundary.
States that only clean (fresh-bit-input-0) columns matter, so arbitrary completions on fresh-bit-input-1 columns are irrelevant.

substantive_reasons: The exact root quantifies arbitrary finite complex square stages U, rectangular cores K and arbitrary complex boundary. Its only logical relation is equality of every fresh-input-bit-zero column to K at every time. Full unitarity, normalization, real amplitudes, support, global-action and completion-existence premises are absent.

Output/input orientation is preserved: U_t[(bit,b),(0,a)] is the local coefficient from old bond a to emitted bit and new bond b. FreshZero zeroes every input-bit-one component; identity on passive prefixes collapses the remaining one-step sum.

Transfer starts at identity and at time n multiplies coreSlice(K_n)(x_n) on the left of transfer(K,n,prefix). Thus the newest slice is leftmost and the earliest stage acts first. No order reversal, conjugation or phase quotient has been introduced.

At n=0 run is the explicit boundary and transfer is identity. The quantification includes zero and unnormalized boundaries. No nonempty B premise is added; with B empty there is no output b, so the coordinatewise assertion is vacuous.
The result is exact complex amplitude equality on the complete word/final-bond basis, including phases. It is not merely a physical-bit marginal, a norm equality or equality up to global phase.

The decoder correctly reconstructs all these facts. The canonical request to state irrelevant columns follows as a direct corollary: two supplied stage sequences with the same zero-input columns and the same K have the same run by applying this equality twice; input-bit-one columns never enter.

views.canonical_question: In the sequential bond construction, suppose every stage matrix is a full unitary on the fresh-bit-and-bond register and the run starts from a single bond basis label (one bond coordinate equal to one, the rest zero). Prove that the total probability (sum of squared amplitude moduli over all basis labels) of the emitted state is exactly one at every length n. Explain why this is a coherent success statement with no postselection, and what role the fresh-zero padding plays.
canonical_assumptions: each stage is a full unitary on the fresh-bit-and-bond register
the run starts from a single bond basis label
canonical_conventions: amplitude mass is sum of star(amplitude) times amplitude; a basis boundary has one unit coordinate
the lifted stage is the Kronecker product of identity on passive wires with the stage

canonical_rubric.criterion: Defines amplitude mass as the sum of star times value and shows a single step factors as fresh-zero padding then a lifted (Kronecker-with-identity) unitary action.
Shows fresh-zero padding is mass-preserving and that a full unitary action preserves mass via star(Mv).(Mv) = star(v).v, hence one step preserves mass.
Inducts on n to conclude the run preserves mass, then evaluates the basis-boundary mass to 1.
Explains this is coherent success with no postselection/renormalization and that fresh-zero padding is a mass-neutral register enlargement.

substantive_reasons: The exact target is an equality in R: the finite sum over PrimitiveBasis(n) times B of Complex.normSq(run amplitude) equals 1. It genuinely uses squared amplitude moduli, not a C-valued amplitudeMass equality relabeled as probability.

The source amplitudeMass is C-valued sum_i star(v_i)*v_i. Its real part is sum_i(Re(v_i)^2+Im(v_i)^2)=sum_i Complex.normSq(v_i). This bridge holds for every finite complex vector without any positivity or normalization premise. Taking real parts of the complex mass-one equality gives the stated real probability root.

The only logical premise is full square-stage unitarity at every natural time. Direct Mathlib source inspection confirms unitary membership consists of both star-product identities; for complex matrices star is conjugate transpose. K, core alignment, support, clean-bond, normalization-as-an-input-assumption, global run-action and completion-existence premises are absent.

The supplied initial:B gives a literal basis boundary and hence inhabitance in every instance. At n=0 the unique empty physical string and this one nonzero bond coordinate give mass 1. The target does not incorrectly assert normalization of an empty-dimensional state or an arbitrary unnormalized boundary.

FreshZero is a mass-neutral embedding into old-word times fresh-bit times bond. The lifted stage is identity on passive emitted wires tensor U; the final Fin.init/Fin.last regrouping is bijective. No branch is discarded, projected or renormalized.

The probability sum retains every physical word and final bond label jointly. It does not select a final bond, prove final-bond cleanup, establish separability, or assert a pure state on physical bits alone. The decoder correctly preserves this boundary.

The canonical all-length total-probability conclusion is therefore matched exactly. The separate explanation of coherence and padding is supported by these definitions/helper mechanisms, but is not a prose answer or proof-method certificate delivered by the scalar root equality alone.
